correctness.rationale: C PASS: The Petersen graph KG(5,2) has graph diameter two. For its symmetric edge polytope, polar extreme potentials have connected tight-edge graph (otherwise componentwise perturbation) and hence all coordinate differences integral; diameter two bounds their normalized values to 0,1,2. Exhaustively checking 3^10=59049 ternary labels with all 15 edge Lipschitz constraints and tight connectedness is therefore a complete finite proof, not statistical sampling. Independent fresh integer enumeration recovered exactly 1410 polar vertices, 11 K=10/d^2 shells and their complete joint table of tight-edge facet-vertex counts, plus all 18 orbits of S5 and central sign. Largest K=56 has 30 facet contacts, next K=49 has 180 11-vertex facets, giving distance gap sqrt(10)/7-sqrt(5/28). All 18 orbits cover the whole integer set without omission; 280 facets have exactly 9 affinely independent vertices and are simplicial.

originality.rationale: O PASS (qualified): The earlier exact Petersen inradius theorem was read in full. It already establishes the very same graph, its 1410 facets, 30 tangent facets and norm maximum 28/5, so none of these are novel. Its full theorem and enumerator do not state the other ten shells, joint 9/10/11/12 face-size counts, first 180 noncontact facets or 18 symmetry orbits. Classical Lipschitz facets and facet-subgraph criteria supply general means of computing such a finite table but not its specific evaluated data. Exact alternative Petersen facet listings or graph-spread tables may exist under different terminology.
residual_risks: Specialist unpublished/supplementary polytope tables or graph-spread metric formulations could already give some/all shells.
Finite exact enumeration is complete only after the graph diameter-two/tight-connectivity reduction, not a theorem for other Kneser graphs.
